channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Strategy Has A 'Fortress Balance Sheet': CEO
item.description: Phong Le, CEO and president of Strategy, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Strategy resumed Bitcoin purchases after a 10-week pause, returning to its signature accumulation strategy after the crypto bear market pressured its shares, weakened confidence in the financing model and prompted a balance-sheet overhaul. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent's 'Bluff' 'Backfired': Pantera's Morehead
item.description: "The only way a bluff works is if nobody at the poker table knows you are bluffing, and to slide an extra $2 billion of poker chips out onto the table...when you are a forced seller...it backfired." Dan Morehead talks about Bessent's bond plan. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pantera's Morehead Talks Bessent's 'Backfire', Bitcoin
item.description: Dan Morehead, founder & managing partner at Pantera Capital joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss US Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond announcement, the future of digital asset treasuries, and crypto trading. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s Compute Bet, Musk on AI, Apple’s New CEO | Bloomberg Tech 9/01/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Anthropic's $35 billion computing deal with Nvidia-backed cloud provider Lambda as the AI startup looks to expand its AI capacity. Plus, Elon Musk predicts AI will increase the global economy by up to 30%. And, John Ternus officially takes over as Apple CEO as the company gets ready for a new product unveil next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Polymarket Valuation Hits $21B, Led By Trump Jr.'s 1789
item.description: Bloomberg's Todd Gillespie joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Venture capital firm 1789 Capital is leading a new funding round for Polymarket that will give the prediction-markets platform a $21 billion post-money valuation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: JPMorgan’s Aliaga Says Market Can Absorb ‘Attractive’ Tech Debt
item.description: JPMorgan Asset Management’s Stephanie Aliaga said that the bond market can absorb the growing supply of hyperscaler debt, as rising artificial intelligence demand reassures investors that the companies can pay their obligations.
item.dc:creator: Ed Ludlow

item.title: LSE to Roll Out Tokenized Stocks
item.description: Amira Valliani, head of payments growth at The Solana Foundation, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." The London Stock Exchange is planning to launch tokenized stocks, backed by shares of London-listed companies, as it looks to further embrace digital assets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hyperliquid In Talks For US Market Entry
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence's Dushyant Shahrawat joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Hyperliquid is in advanced talks to bring its perpetual futures to US traders through Kraken’s parent company Payward, just weeks after President Trump said his administration was working to bring the fast-growing platform into the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s 2,300% Rally Under Tim Cook
item.description: Tim Cook hands the reins of Apple to John Ternus after a 15-year run that transformed the company into a $4.6 trillion giant and delivered a nearly 2,300% stock gain. Bloomberg’s Ryan Vlastelica looks at Cook’s market legacy and why Apple shares are increasingly moving against the broader AI trade. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sold 'Minuscule' Amount of Bitcoin: Strategy CEO
item.description: Phong Le, CEO and president of Strategy, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Strategy resumed Bitcoin purchases after a 10-week pause, returning to its signature accumulation strategy after the crypto bear market pressured its shares, weakened confidence in the financing model and prompted a balance-sheet overhaul. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dyson Unveils AI-Powered Toothbrush With Built-In Camera
item.description: Dyson introduced a $499 toothbrush that uses AI and a built-in camera to give real-time feedback. The toothbrush, called CameraJet, is the first with an integrated camera to narrow in on the gaps in the teeth and direct a precision jet at them. Bloomberg's Sam Kelly joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ternus Takes Apple Helm Ahead of Foldable iPhone Debut
item.description: John Ternus begins his first day as Apple CEO as the company prepares for one of its biggest product launches in years. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman explains how the longtime hardware chief will manage Apple’s veteran leadership team and what to expect from the company’s first foldable iPhone, including a price tag above $2,000. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can the US AI Boom Survive Data Center Backlash?
item.description: Data centers are emerging as an issue in political races across the US as voters raise concerns about power costs and the rapid AI infrastructure buildout. Information Technology Industry Council CEO Jason Oxman discusses the tech industry’s response, growing calls to restrict new projects, and why continued investment is critical to competing with China in AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Says New Fable 5.1 AI Model Is Cheaper, Better at Coding
item.description: Anthropic PBC is releasing a new version of its powerful Fable artificial intelligence model that it says is better at coding and science tasks, as well as more economical — all changes it says are in response to customer feedback.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Nestle Sells Vitamins Business to PE Buyer for $1 Billion
item.description: Nestle SA plans to sell its mainstream vitamins and supplements business to US private equity firm Yellow Wood Partners for $1 billion as Chief Executive Officer Philipp Navratil tries to streamline and turn around the Swiss foodmaker.
item.dc:creator: Sonja Wind and Fabienne Kinzelmann

item.title: Apple Ternus Touts Product Pipeline, ‘Phenomenal’ Sept. 9 iPhone Launch in Memo
item.description: Apple Inc. Chief Executive Officer John Ternus touted the company’s strong product pipeline and teased a “phenomenal” iPhone launch next week in his first remarks to employees as their new leader.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: JPMorgan's Aliaga Is Upbeat on Demand for Big-Tech Debt
item.description: Big Tech is increasingly turning to debt to finance the massive buildout of AI infrastructure. JPMorgan Asset Management's global market strategist Stephanie Aliaga explains why hyperscaler bond issuance is poised to keep growing, how the market is absorbing the new supply, and why stronger visibility into AI returns could help sustain the spending boom. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Tech Is Incapable of Solving Its Own Problem, Says Mukunda
item.description:
Bill Gates, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp., published a 6,000-word essay on Aug. 26 saying that he would slow the development of artificial intelligence if he could. He elaborated in an interview with the New York Times, saying “in private, people who understand how good this stuff is, and how much better it’s getting, they’re very worried” but few are raising the issues in public.
The public is already convinced the tech industry can’t be trusted with its own creations. Some legal news last week explains why. A bipartisan coalition of 51 attorneys general announced a proposed settlement with Meta Platforms Inc. that obligates the social media company that runs Facebook and Instagram to put tight restrictions on how children use its platforms.
Gautam Mukunda, Lecturer at the Yale School of Management and Bloomberg Opinion contributor, joins Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s Ternus Era Begins After Tim Cook Delivers 2,300% Stock Gain
item.description:
Apple Inc.’s Tim Cook handed over the reins to John Ternus on Tuesday, capping a tenure as chief executive officer that cemented the company as an iconic global brand and turned its stock into one of the most reliable bets.
The shares soared 2,258% under Cook, who took over from legendary founder Steve Jobs after the close of trading on Aug. 24, 2011. Cook inherited a company with a market capitalization of less than $350 billion and built the maker of iPhones and Mac computers into a diverse $4.6 trillion business that also sells watches, AirPods, and financial services.
For more on what lies ahead for both Ternus and the tech giant, we speak with Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Global Consumer Tech. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Signs $35 Billion Pact With Nvidia-Backed Lambda
item.description: Anthropic PBC agreed to a $35 billion computing deal with Lambda, a cloud provider backed by Nvidia Corp., part of an effort to quickly expand its AI capacity, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford
